A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOH benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and generation experiments, factual-change extraction evaluations, and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendices A–E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds manual QA validation, temporal retrieval comparisons, and GPT-4o experiments.

M1.justification: The factual-change extraction, Qwen-based screening, QA generation and review, monthly updating, and temporally weighted search procedures remain unchanged. The added human audit is described as an additional validation experiment.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same June–November 2024 Wikipedia-derived benchmark, containing 96,124 questions and 219,463 documents. Dataset domains and passage scenarios remain unchanged; the new evaluations use subsets of existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the evaluated comparison methods by adding MRAG and TempRALM for both BGE embeddings in Table 15 and GPT-4o for generation in Tables 16–17. All original comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds a GPT-4o evaluation on 1,000 test samples and a random 500-QA human audit using four quality criteria. The original 10,000-question evaluation, metrics, and passage configurations remain unchanged; these are additional experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds direct human validation of final QA quality, distinct from the retained checks of factual-change extraction and response judging. Appendix E.3 also extends controlled passage-type and ordering sensitivity analyses to GPT-4o, materially broadening the validation and robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new human audit reports accuracy percentages without adding uncertainty or annotator-agreement estimates.

E6.justification: Matched original results are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table 9 reports QA-quality accuracies of 100.0%, 99.2%, 98.4%, and 100.0%. Table 15 reports BGE-M3 relevant/outdated hit rates at 5 of 0.3183/0.0574 for MRAG versus baseline 0.7312/0.5507. Tables 16–17 add GPT-4o results, including scores of 89.5 with one relevant and one distracting passage versus 65.5 with one relevant and one outdated passage under relevance ordering.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of extraction and updating, retrieval metric, and Appendix A.2 processing-time analysis remain unchanged. No new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about HOH, scalable dataset construction, and outdated information harming retrieval and generation. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E extends the retrieval tradeoff interpretation to MRAG and TempRALM and the generator-vulnerability interpretation to GPT-4o. It also compares GPT-4o with Llama-70B, although matched-subset Llama results are not reported. Section 7's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds an explicit code-and-data availability statement and repository link; v1 only mentions an open-source repository without that access pointer. Existing implementation settings and prompts remain unchanged, and detailed configurations for the new temporal methods and GPT-4o are not supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly positions the benchmark against MRAG and TempRALM as existing temporal retrieval solutions. The background section and bibliography are otherwise substantively retained; the new methods have unresolved question-mark citations, leaving their exact sources unidentified.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording edits, a revised Section 4.3 heading, acknowledgments, and an expanded Appendix E with separate retrieval and generation subsections. The overall narrative remains intact, but v2 introduces unresolved citations and leaves an 'adjust model names' editing note in Appendix E.3.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables for manual validation, temporal retrieval, and GPT-4o results, with corresponding redistribution and renumbering of appendix tables. Table 1's caption clarifies that question counts exclude time-irrelevant questions. Existing figures and display formats are retained.

improvement.justification: The new human audit directly supports final QA quality, while temporal retrieval and GPT-4o experiments broaden support for the existing findings. The repository pointer also improves access information. These gains outweigh localized shortcomings, but their benefit is limited by missing experimental details, unmatched samples in the GPT-4o/Llama comparison, unresolved citations, an editing note, and Appendix D.5's retained statement that no closed-source models were tested.
